title: Personal take on why OSS should not pay rent
why: Author built many OSS repos earning almost nothing; advises keeping a full-time job and treating OSS as a side pursuit.

title: Why Ruby may lose startup mindshare to ecosystems
why: Startups pick Rails for its ecosystem, not Ruby itself; the commenter argues Ruby's metaprogramming and MRI limits will reduce its use.

title: Why SOPA-style enforcement is unnecessary for copyright
why: Argues DMCA safe harbors already balance infringement enforcement, so SOPA-style laws are an overreach rather than a requirement.

title: Factorio as a lesson in logistics
why: Enthusiastic game review; praises how automation exposes real-world logistics complexity, but offers little transferable technical substance.

title: Critique of Ethereum merge decentralization
why: Opinion that staking still concentrates control among large players, and that human intervention layers exclude smaller participants.

title: Why officials seem to know what they do
why: Anecdotal opinion from a public-sector insider that decisions look sensible from the decision-makers' perspective, without a concrete mechanism.

title: Why GNOME uses instant-apply configuration design
why: Explains GNOME's instant-apply settings choice, which drives a configuration service that notifies apps of changes, and the alt-drag workaround for panels.

title: Why DNS over HTTPS leaks to ISPs anyway
why: DoH sends queries to one resolver, and IPs and SNI stay unencrypted, so ISPs still see destinations; gives how to block DoH endpoints.

title: Self-promotion for an Erlang web platform
why: Announces a personal Erlang and CoffeeScript web framework project and argues for parallel execution, with little substantive explanation.

title: Argument against suppressing harmful discussion
why: Philosophical argument that censoring discussion removes error correction, so one cannot discover being wrong; reply to a specific thread.

title: Anecdote on Lehman Brothers and Dick Fuld
why: Second-hand account of Lehman's collapse with unverifiable claims about banks and regulators; no checkable explanation of mechanisms.

title: Personal story of quitting a job
why: Personal career anecdote about money mistakes and downward mobility; warnings are emotional rather than instructive for technical readers.

title: Detecting dead-code benchmark cheating in browsers
why: Shows a method to spot a browser optimizing away unused benchmark code, by inserting an early return and comparing timing changes across engines.

title: How ILR proficiency levels assess spoken language
why: Expert rubric-based assessment using ILR levels, separating pronunciation from discourse, circumlocution and sustained communication when judging a speaker's Mandarin.

title: Real monthly costs of living in Bangkok
why: Firsthand budget figures for Bangkok apartments and food, showing it is not as cheap as assumed; useful but personal rather than technical.

title: Critique of Scala as a practical language
why: Opinionated rant that Scala masquerades as well designed; argues language constraints matter, citing Rich Hickey's instrument analogy.

title: Why a storage system chose Rust over Go
why: Explains heap-size-driven choice of Rust: bit-packing, perfect hashing, stack allocation and FFI, with GC pauses irrelevant for non-latency-sensitive workloads.

title: Mutable and immutable variables are equivalent under SSA
why: Shows that in a single execution, mutable reassignment can be rewritten as SSA fresh variables, so the mutable/immutable distinction is not observable.

title: Personal preference for Apple Maps over Google
why: Subjective impressions of routing quality, such as unsafe side-road routes and noisy alerts, without measurable data or technical explanation.

title: Expectations for junior engineer ramp-up
why: Advice to a struggling junior: productivity typically takes about a year, and seniors expect to give input. Addressed to one person, so context-bound.

title: Pitch for discovery-based content search
why: Startup pitch distinguishing known-item search from discovery recommendation, with claims about a new UI and data; promotional, not substantive.

title: How the DES cracker book evaded export controls
why: Historical account: the EFF book printed DES cracker source as scannable, checksummed text, exploiting the paper publishing exception to circumvent digital export restrictions.

title: Satirical checklist against a new language
why: Humorous checklist mocking language design proposals; the content is satire rather than an explanation a reader could learn from.

title: Measuring run queue latency with runqlat histograms
why: Run queue latency is the key scheduler metric; a BPF histogram shows how long runnable threads wait, exposing scheduling bugs that averages hide.

title: Argument that crypto donations offset taxes
why: Speculative tax argument with rough numbers about crypto donations and capital gains; the author admits the figures were wrong.

title: Why the NRA beats privacy advocates
why: Political argument comparing membership and voting power of gun owners and privacy groups; not technical.

title: Personal liability for unpaid withheld payroll taxes
why: Explains IRC 6672: withheld payroll taxes are held in trust, so any responsible officer can face personal liability for the full amount.

title: Why single-viewer streams can count as public performance
why: Explains the public performance doctrine: one owned copy repeatedly shown to individual patrons in private rooms was held a public performance in Redd Horne.

title: Why mainframes sell reliability and high-volume transactions
why: Insider explanation: mainframes target near-zero downtime for many short transactions, such as card validation, where economies depend on uninterrupted service.

title: Corporations, not open source, are the funding problem
why: Argues that open source failure is really corporate free-riding, comparing it to hunters overhunting ducks; a framing argument rather than new information.

title: How a typography book could earn more
why: Business analysis comparing traffic and book revenue to a similar blog; estimates are anecdotal and the lessons are marketing-specific.

title: Personal story of a gifted childhood
why: Anecdote about accelerated math and social isolation as a gifted child; personal rather than instructive.

title: Complaint about closed consumer electronics
why: Argues that consumers cannot buy open hardware without a large premium; a demand and opinion, with no technical explanation.

title: Personal claim that diet cured ADHD
why: Anecdotal self-experiment with a paleo diet; not controlled evidence and not generalizable.

title: Checklist for judging experimental claims
why: Applies Norvig's warning signs for experiment design, such as lack of randomized controlled trials, as a practical checklist for evaluating health claims.

title: Why automakers struggle with open source software
why: Insider account: open source offers no indemnity to big firms, SYNC avoided Windows, and maps and parts came from outside partners.

title: Opinion on Snowden and public attitudes
why: Political opinion on surveillance and Snowden's prosecution, with anecdotes about conversations; no technical content.

title: Call for economic strategy during lockdown
why: Opinion arguing that shelter-in-place needs an exit strategy and weighing economic externalities; policy opinion without technical substance.

title: Freelancer, contractor and consultant are different relationships
why: Distinguishes three client relationships by who sets strategy, and notice periods, so you can price and set expectations for each role.

title: Reflection on chess as a time sink
why: Personal reflection that playing chess mainly improves chess; a colleague's comment shapes the author's views, with no technical lesson.

title: Moderator policy on follow-up stories
why: Moderator note explaining how HN downweights follow-ups without significant new information during major ongoing topics; policy, not a learnable technique.

title: Argument for terminal editors over IDEs
why: Opinion that Vim with LSP and clangd gives most IDE features over SSH; personal preference, though it offers some setup detail.

title: Argument defending non-compete agreements
why: Meta-argument about argument from ignorance, then a defense of non-competes via contract freedom and local knowledge; opinion, not a mental model learners can apply.

title: Developer complaints about Microsoft stack
why: List of grievances about Virtual PC, Windows lock-in and SQL Server Linux drivers; complaint-driven rather than instructive.

title: Why asteroid mining economics do not add up
why: Walks through delta-V, launch cost, and extraction constraints to show why valuable asteroid material would lose value once supply floods the market.

title: Listing a non-programmer co-founder's duties
why: Describes non-technical startup tasks such as accounting, marketing and payroll; a list of duties without deeper explanation.

title: Rebuttal of MBA hiring signal argument
why: Opinion defending MBAs against an earlier essay, with insults and anecdote; no transferable technical knowledge.

title: Frustration with 2FA and account recovery
why: Rant about SMS MFA and lockouts, calling for standardized login; complaint with a general lesson but little detail.

title: Defense of Richard Stallman and the FSF
why: Defends RMS and FSF's influence and links to the E-Parasites censorship debate; opinion and personal rant.

title: Roman jokes collected from sources
why: A list of ancient Roman jokes; entertaining but not an explanation of anything technical or insightful.

title: Stay-at-home dad faces park hostility
why: Personal account of being harassed at parks and libraries; experience-based but not technical, and no transferable lesson for technical readers.

title: Launch post for a 3D website builder
why: Product launch describing an open-source three.js framework and no-code 3D editor; promotional content.

title: Proposal to fix debt via rates and money printing
why: Economic argument about mortgage debt and rates; contested macro opinion with a hypothetical example and no grounded evidence.

title: Apple bundled apps have always been weak
why: Personal take that Apple's bundled applications were never the best; the commenter uses Google and third-party apps instead.

title: Choose a license that matches your intent
why: Persuasive advice: permissive licenses allow anyone to profit, so pick GPL or MPL if you want reciprocity. Opinion-driven, though the consequences are concrete.

title: Personal story of isolation and heroin relapse
why: Personal, emotional account of loneliness and addiction; no learnable technical content.

title: Practical reasons to choose OCaml
why: Experienced perspective on OCaml's labeled arguments, dual compilation modes and JS backend, though mostly preference and comparison rather than a deep explanation.

title: Use version control for legislation
why: Proposes git-based bill tracking for transparency and blame; a creative idea, but a proposal rather than an explanation.

title: Personal account of declining intelligence in college
why: Anecdote about sleepiness and falling grades; no explanation or actionable lesson given.

title: Why infringement is not theft in law
why: Explains that theft and copyright infringement are distinct legal categories, both framed as alienable rights, which makes the stealing debate legally irrelevant.

title: Argument that long hours can be rational
why: Opinion pushing back on a book's pitch about overwork, citing personal projects and rational trade-offs; not technical.

title: Running Kubernetes requires dedicated operations staff
why: First-hand account: migrating a pipeline to Kubernetes without ops expertise caused constant firefighting, and managed EKS upgrades were risky; serverless was simpler.

title: Rebuttal to article on working less
why: Angry rebuttal listing successful people who worked long hours; argumentative and ad hominem, with no technical content.

title: Critique of proposed Python 2.8
why: Argues that porting debt is the user's responsibility and that a Python 2.8 would produce subtly divergent behavior; opinion-heavy.

title: Request for nbench results on a C1 board
why: Asks for a benchmark run and pastes comparison numbers for other hardware; little explanation of what the results mean.

title: Canada dropped the penny without fuss
why: Anecdotal opinion that Canada's penny removal went smoothly and that sales tax rounding should use multiples of five; policy opinion.

title: Argument about skeuomorphism and macOS icons
why: Opinion on skeuomorphic icons and hidden UI controls, defending Jobs and modern flat design; subjective, not instructive.

title: Argument against teaching students Eclipse
why: Opinion that beginners should use IDE wizards and Stack Overflow rather than learn build internals, plus a point on char versus UTF-8.

title: Argument that piracy beats streaming services
why: Opinion favoring piracy for quality, convenience and sharing, with the author's own edits; a debate stance rather than explanation.

title: Critique of Alameda insolvency speculation
why: Argues insolvency cannot be judged without knowing collateralized liabilities; a rebuttal of journalism, but it lacks a clear reusable explanation.

title: Mexican identity and the word Western
why: Personal cultural identity essay about whether Mexicans count as Western; opinion with no technical content.

title: Why elites turn toward surveillance
why: Political opinion on democracy disillusionment and social media chaos; sweeping claims without evidence.

title: Experience running large call centers
why: Firsthand call-center experience: queues of hundreds of customers at scale, so automation follows. Insightful, but it is a rebuttal to a complaint.

title: Why Apple's App Store trademark is weak
why: Explains trademark registrability: generic terms cannot be registered, and the arbitrary-meaning argument for app is the key legal question.

title: Newspaper lies and the narrative problem
why: Anecdotes of media fabrication around a bus bombing and a cannabis story; opinion about narratives, with no technical knowledge.

title: Context on a misremembered HN comment
why: Moderator context defending a 2007 comment about file sync; a historical correction about a specific thread, not a broader lesson.

title: Dark mode CSS for Hacker News
why: Shares a dark-mode stylesheet for HN using media queries; a niche snippet rather than an explanation of general technique.

title: Defending dishwasher Wi-Fi update prompts
why: Personal account of a Miele dishwasher's update prompt, VLAN setup and Home Assistant; niche and product-specific.

title: Rebuttal on Chinese debt in Africa
why: Argues about debt levels and Chinese projects in East Africa; political claims with some figures but no clear technical lesson.

title: Wishlist of abandoned software to revive
why: Wish list naming Windows Phone, Image Composer and desktop email clients; opinion about the value of on-device computing.

title: German views on Facebook currency
why: Cultural and historical perspective on German resistance to centralized power and private currencies; political opinion.

title: Why JavaScript not Python or Lua won the browser
why: Insider explanation: mid-1990s Python and Lua could not change incompatibly for browsers, so JS evolved in standards, with interoperation requirements driving its spec.

title: Moderator note on repetitive political stories
why: Moderator explanation of how repetitive follow-up stories harm curiosity; policy rather than technical knowledge.

title: Why parties sorted by issues, not extremity
why: Political science: polarization comes from issue positions aligning with party, shown by southern conservative Democrats re-registering as Republicans through inertia.

title: Call for individual climate action
why: Emotional plea for HN readers to change personal habits, such as flying less; a call to action rather than explanation.

title: You cannot optimize every life area at once
why: Personal advice: focus energy on one area at a time and maintain others; sensible but anecdotal and not technical.

title: Argument on not making China an enemy
why: Political opinion that totalitarian regimes need an external enemy; a rhetorical argument without evidence.

title: How a small fiber ISP is actually built
why: Firsthand guide: pick a backhaul point, run fiber to customers, and work around rights of way and monopoly rules; money is the main barrier.

title: Argument that open source cannot fund compilers
why: Argues open-source licenses cannot fund paid engineers, using Java and Oracle, and promotes the author's own funding need; partisan.

title: Criticism of a student's school explosion
why: Moral judgment of a student's school chemistry experiment and media coverage; opinion, not technical.

title: Running Windows gaming in a VM via GPU passthrough
why: Practical setup: IOMMU lets a VM get exclusive PCI-E GPU access, so Linux hosts can run Windows gaming VMs without dual boot.

title: Defense of R for non-programmers
why: Opinion that R is easier for analysts than Python thanks to RStudio and fungible vectors; partisan comparison with some concrete examples.

title: Personal discovery of a live-in housekeeper
why: Personal account of discovering a housekeeper's conditions abroad; moral reflection, not technical.

title: Cloud repatriation is limited by lost skills
why: Insight from a thesis: the main barrier to leaving the cloud is de-skilling, since staff can no longer run buffers and transcoders on-prem.

title: Argument that trust in authorities matters
why: Opinion that education beats coercion and that lost trust is the real cost of censorship; philosophical argument without evidence.

title: Concern that simulations may be chaotic
why: Raises concerns that iterative simulations can be chaotic and buggy, so results may reflect researcher selection; a worry, not a worked explanation.

title: Why hospitals struggle to publish price data
why: Insider explanation: health systems are fragmented medical malls running legacy systems like Epic and MUMPS, so pricing data is scattered across many sources.

title: Rebuttal of infrastructure bankruptcy claims
why: Argues road maintenance is a small share of city budgets and cities have not gone bankrupt; a counter-argument with limited data.

title: Angry account of Oakland gentrification protest
why: Hostile political rant about protesters and gentrification; not technical.

title: Observations on school social spheres
why: Opinion on US school social groups and innovators; anecdotal sociology without evidence.
